transcript: Yeah, so I ranked these societies this way because I do feel like for number one, modern green utopia, I think that's an achievable balance that everybody wants, you know, where there's just more sustainable technology being used and we're living in harmony with the environment and still maintaining earth because as time goes on that is a huge concern is taking care of the planet and making sure that we can live here for another you know million for for as long as we can as a human um society the second one i put um was a moral commonwealth um so just like in immorality I do feel like um certain cultures like a Japan they have that and they operate for at least from like a social standpoint I feel like they operate well within each other there's respect there's discipline there's honor and I think a society like that really would be beneficial, and it would allow people to come together. The futuristic utopia, sometimes that feels like that's where we are headed. It does feel like technology is just rapidly advancing, and just that is the main focus. It's like, okay, let's just make the next best thing to advance society. And I do think if we're able to harness that power, then yes, that is a super exciting future that I think a lot of us would want to live in. I think of that as like almost like a Jetsons scenario where it's just like you see all this cool technology coincide with human existence. and for fourth i had religious utopia mainly because that does seem like that's how things were back in the day it seems like there was more togetherness because of that as a society when religion was the cornerstone or foundation upon which everybody um got together and and um were a part of so there was more unity there and it just seemed like um from the standpoint of just environment and you know the rest of the world there wasn't you know a lot of besides wars there wasn't a lot of um misuse of the planet because of that and it's it's more simplistic there is less technology there is less outside influence on judgment and everything is based off of one religious text and the morality behind that. The next, I put a pre-visit utopia, so low-tech, small-scale. And this would just be, again, if I could think of a time period before that, this would be almost like a pre-'90s where it's just like, okay, you know what? Maybe we don't need all of this tech. and if we do need it we don't need it on like a massive scale we just need it to to do the bare minimum and then we can thrive with ourselves as humans um again that does seem like a step backwards um to some degree but it does seem like a simpler way to live and then the next option which I don't like at all um which is pretty much just having the institutions rule rule over everyone um and they're basically having those just the final say the final um go ahead for everything um you just have a lot of power in the few um individuals and i don't think that's um ideal at all and the next is the ai center utopia where basically ai controls and governs us. And I think that's a scary society to live in when humans are no longer in control of just humans and have human inputs. Now we've put it into this essentially digital God that's been created to enforce and regulate everything like we were animals. And that's something that I don't necessarily agree with. I think humans should deal with human situation. There's no problem with having tech aid in that, but I do think humans should always make the final decision on humans.
